summarize_policy.original: Summarize the following refund policy in three sentences: Customers may return unopened items within 30 days of purchase for a full refund. Opened items are eligible for store credit only, valid for 12 months. Items marked final sale cannot be returned under any circumstances.
variants: In three sentences, provide a summary of this returns policy: Unopened products can be sent back within a month of buying for a complete refund. If the packaging has been opened, only store credit is given, and it stays valid for one year. Any product labelled as a final sale is non-returnable.

Please condense the following return policy into three sentences: A full refund is available for unopened items returned within 30 days. Store credit lasting 12 months is the only option for opened items. Final sale items are excluded from all returns.

Summarise this policy in 3 sentences — Refund policy: returns of sealed goods within thirty days get a full refund; opened goods get store credit valid for a year; items sold as final sale are not eligible for return under any condition.

Can you give me a three-sentence summary of the following? Our policy allows full refunds on unopened returns within 30 days of purchase. Once opened, items may only be exchanged for store credit, which expires after 12 months. Products designated as final sale are strictly non-refundable.

multi_step_calculation.original: A store had 240 units of inventory. They sold 35% in week one, then restocked 50 units, then sold 20% of the new total in week two. How many units remain?
variants: A shop started with 240 items in stock. During the first week, 35 percent of the stock was sold. Afterwards, 50 more units were added. In the second week, 20 percent of the updated stock was sold. What is the remaining stock count?
Inventory problem: begin with 240 units. Sell 35% in week 1. Add 50 units. Then sell 20% of whatever is left. How many units do you end up with?
Start: 240 units. Week 1: sell 35% of stock. Restock: add 50 units. Week 2: sell 20% of current stock. Final inventory?

A retailer has 240 units. In the first week they moved 35% of inventory. They then received a shipment of 50 units. The following week they sold a fifth of their current stock. How many units are left after both weeks?
